draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Srirangapatna! This island town in the Kaveri was Tipu Sultan's fortress capital, and it was here, in the siege of 1799, that he fell and the British took Mysore.
draft.hungryLine: For a cheap, early breakfast, the small cafes by the KSRTC bus station are your best bet.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The Ranganathaswamy Temple is a 10 min walk, the Garrison Cemetery about 14 min, and Tipu Sultan Fort about 16 min.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Find the little riverside seats near Wellesley Bridge, by the Anjaneya Swamy Temple. It's a peaceful spot to watch the river for an hour or two.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The Garrison Cemetery holds about 307 graves from the 1799 assault, and 80 of them are officers of a Swiss regiment, the de Meuron Regiment.

spots.name: Ranganathaswamy Temple
spots.detail: 10 min walk · Vishnu reclining on the serpent Ananta

spots.name: Garrison Cemetery
spots.detail: 14 min walk · Graves from the 1799 siege, by the river

spots.name: Tipu Sultan Fort
spots.detail: 16 min walk · Tipu's fort, with dungeons and the breach

legends.title: Prisoners in the water
legends.body: It's said British prisoners here were chained to the stone and kept in water up to their necks. Colonel William Baillie was held here and died in 1782.

legends.title: The deserted bungalow
legends.body: This riverside house of Colonel Scott, who fought in the 1799 siege, is tied to a local legend and tragedy. An 1875 poem, The Deserted Bungalow, mourns its fate.

tips.title: Do the summer palace first.
tips.body: Daria Daulat Bagh is open 9AM to 4PM, while the Gumbaz stays open until 6PM.

tips.title: Time your mosque visit.
tips.body: At Masjid-e-Ala, go right after the call to prayer to see the inner hall open, and take off your shoes at the steps.

story.title: The temple town
story.body: The Ranganathaswamy Temple was consecrated around 984 CE, and the town takes its name from it.

story.title: A fort on the island
story.body: Timmanna Nayaka built the fort in 1454. Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan later strengthened it with help from French architects.

story.title: Mysore takes over
story.body: Raja Wodeyar I defeated the Vijayanagara viceroy here in 1610 and celebrated Navaratri in the town that year.

story.title: The final siege
story.body: The British and their allies breached the walls on 4 May 1799. Tipu Sultan died in the battle, and the Wadiyars were put back on the Mysore throne.

story.title: The Obelisk
story.body: Krishna Raja Wadiyar IV built the Obelisk Monument in 1907 to remember those who died in the siege.
